units.translation: ⟦1⟧ with dative as at ⟦2⟧ etc., under the influence of something; the ⟦3⟧ is the ruin that clings to him from his guilt, which robs him of clear consciousness; immediately it is also compared to a darkness in which one cannot see. Cf. on 378 ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧; here, however, ⟦6⟧ (the blood-guilt) is the actual subject, and ⟦7⟧ is predicative. On 379 cf. ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧;
For some Stygian mist hovers over
sunless, mortal-hating darknesses cover the house
⟦1⟧ is the speech of the people, like ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧ middle instead of ⟦4⟧, as at ⟦5⟧. 852 etc.

The iambic rhythms that stand out from what precedes are generally clear: two acatalectic dimeters with suppressed arsis in the middle and then a similarly constructed catalectic one, thus ending: CICITči,CICI LUI, CICI - -; then three acatalectic dimeters without syncopated interior and again a catalectic one of the same construction as before; the strophe closes with a dactylic pentameter and a trochaic colon, as already noted above. So Rossbach-Westphal. Some details, however, still require discussion.

⟦1⟧ at the beginning of the third colon need not be, as Wecklein correctly observes, (antistrophe ⟦2⟧), since ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ – – – and also probably 1459 ⟦5⟧ is measured. But at the beginning of the fourth colon there is indeed in strophe and antistrophe - - -, cf. on ⟦6⟧ p. 77.

At v. 387 ⟦1⟧ is transmitted, in the corresponding 395 ⟦2⟧; for this, therefore, Hermann wrote ⟦3⟧, since as ⟦4⟧ are used side by side by Aeschylus, so alongside ⟦5⟧ there is a place, cf. ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧. Conversely Wieseler, Dindorf ⟦8⟧ӑ⟦9⟧ for ⟦10⟧, with bad rhythms and without decisive proofs against the spondaic word-form (see below). Hereupon follows in the strophe, as the beginning of the dactylic verse, ⟦11⟧, in the antistrophe regularly ⟦12⟧. Is it a tribrach instead of a dactyl? Is it a prosodic license? Is corruption to be assumed? ⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧ is still easier than ⟦15⟧ -, since the former can attach itself to ⟦16⟧, ⟦17⟧; but a tribrach instead of a dactyl seems to exist in Euripides (Phoen. 796 ⟦18⟧ = 813 ⟦19⟧), yet is not easily to be attributed to Aeschylus. Therefore emendation; see below. Somewhat anomalous is the syllaba anceps at the end of the pentapody: ⟦20⟧ | ⟦21⟧..; for usually the trochaic colon is closely connected, in strophe and antistrophe d even with word-sharing. One could therefore emend: ⟦22⟧ (⟦23⟧) ⟦24⟧. See, however, on ⟦25⟧, where I conversely remove the synapheia by change. V. 381 ff.
